scope_statement.text: Covers detailing of in-situ corbels, beam half joints and continuous nibs. Closely related to joint design; designer must ensure detail design is clearly specified. Does not cover all aspects of precast corbels/half joints/nibs. Bearing pad design is out of scope.

member_types.description: Short cantilever projection from a column/wall face used to support a bearing load (e.g. a beam end).

member_types.name: Half joint (beam)
member_types.description: A stepped/notched end of a beam that provides a reduced-depth bearing seat for a supported member.

member_types.name: Continuous nib
member_types.description: A linear (continuous, not discrete) projection along a beam or wall used as a bearing seat, e.g. for slabs or brickwork support.

column-interface zone (tension lap, compression anchorage, two column links)
body zone (secondary horizontal reinforcement/links, compression bars)
half_joint: bearing/nib root zone (tension anchorage, hanger links at 450, cranked-bar lap)

corbel_to_column.reinforcement_interaction: Corbel main tensile reinforcement lapped in tension into column reinforcement at the corbel/column interface; two additional column links placed close to corbel top; compression bars given compression anchorage into column.

nib_to_supporting_beam.reinforcement_interaction: The vertical leg of the links in the supporting beam must be designed to carry the loads from the nib; effective depth d of the beam should be reduced because concrete in the nib below the vertical beam link does not contribute to resistance.

nib_to_supported_member.reinforcement_interaction: Minimum nominal overlap of 60mm between reinforcement in the nib and reinforcement in the supported member (MN1).

detailing_sequence_implied: 1. Establish concrete grade (≥28/35) and member geometry (corbel projection / half-joint step / nib depth, min 140mm for shallow nib MN2).
2. Establish nominal cover (internal/external, corbel vs. nib/half-joint values) per exposure class.
3. Check minimum reinforcement area (tension As,min, compression Asc,min for corbels; As,min for half joints/nibs).
4. Select main tensile reinforcement arrangement: small-diameter bars/U-bars/easy-bend links preferred; large diameter + welding (MCB2) only if loading/geometry demands.
5. Provide compression bars/anchorage and secondary horizontal reinforcement/links (≥0.5× main tensile area).
6. Place two column links close to corbel top (corbel case).
7. Check bar spacing (min pitch 75mm; min vertical spacing 25mm/bar size; nib max pitch rules by zone).
8. Check anchorage (min 10⌀ or 100mm; Table 6.12 for specific lengths) and laps (tension lap at column/support interface; 60mm min overlap for nibs).
9. Confirm edge distances to bearing (bar diameter or 0.75×cover, whichever greater).

decision_rules.rule: IF member is a corbel/half-joint/nib THEN concrete grade shall not normally be lower than 28/35 MPa (cylinder/cube).
IF corbel is for internal use THEN nominal cover = 25mm + Δcdev (XC1). IF for external use THEN nominal cover = 35mm + Δcdev (XC3).
IF continuous nib or slab half joint is for internal use THEN cover = 20mm or bar size (whichever greater). IF external use THEN cover = 40mm.
IF nominal cover to grouped bars is being detailed THEN use the cover for the equivalent bar size (per 5.8, general chapter).
IF nominal cover exceeds 40mm AND 4-hour fire resistance is required THEN supplementary reinforcement may be required (axis distance to main reinforcement exceeds 70mm).
IF designing corbel tension reinforcement THEN As,min ≥ 0.0014·bt·d.
IF designing corbel compression reinforcement THEN Asc,min ≥ 0.002·Ac.
IF designing half-joint/nib tension reinforcement for Grade 28/35 concrete and fyk=500 THEN As,min = 0.0014·bt·d (else use general formula As,min = 0.26·bt·d·fctm/fyk ≥ 0.0013·bt·d).
IF selecting bar diameter for half joint/nib main reinforcement THEN preferred minimum diameter = 10mm.
IF spacing bars requiring poker-vibrator access THEN minimum pitch = 75mm.
IF bars are vertically stacked THEN minimum vertical space between individual bars = 25mm or bar size, whichever greater.
IF continuous nib main bars are in a general (non-concentrated-load) area THEN max pitch = 3h ≤ 400mm. IF in a concentrated-load area THEN max pitch = 2h ≤ 250mm.
IF continuous nib secondary bars are in a general area THEN max pitch = 3.5h ≤ 450mm. IF in a concentrated-load area THEN max pitch = 3h ≤ 400mm.
IF anchoring any bar in this topic THEN minimum anchorage length = greater of (10 × bar diameter) or 100mm.

IF selecting bar diameters for corbels/half joints/nibs in general THEN small diameters (≤16mm) should be used; IF larger diameters are used THEN welding is likely required, and this should normally be done off-site under factory conditions.

IF detailing corbel main tensile reinforcement THEN small bar diameters, horizontal U-bars or links with easy bends are preferred (Model Detail MCB1). IF loading is high and geometry restrictive THEN large diameter bars may be necessary, requiring welding to a cross bar/plate (Model Detail MCB2), sized to weld strength.

IF detailing corbel main tensile reinforcement THEN it must extend as close to the outer face of the corbel as possible AND extend beyond the load-bearing area by at least the Model-Detail-specified minimum distance.
IF large horizontal forces must be transmitted into a corbel THEN a welded joint may be the only suitable solution.

IF detailing half joints in beams THEN inclined bars provide better crack control than other reinforcement arrangements, BUT they are often difficult to fix and can cause congestion — great care is needed, especially with large bar diameters and welded solutions.

IF detailing continuous nibs THEN vertical U-bars or links should be used wherever possible (Model Detail MN1). IF a shallow nib is required (e.g. to support brickwork) THEN horizontal U-bars should be used instead (Model Detail MN2).

IF detailing a continuous nib THEN the vertical leg of the links in the SUPPORTING beam must be designed to carry the loads from the nib, AND the effective depth d of that beam must be reduced because concrete in the nib below the vertical beam link does not contribute to resistance.
IF horizontal movement may occur between a nib and the supported member THEN the outer edge of the nib should be given a 20mm chamfer.
IF detailing edge distance from bearing to reinforcement (Model Details MCB1/MHJ/MN1) THEN distance = minimum of (bar diameter) or (0.75 × cover), whichever is GREATER.

IF detailing Model Detail MCB1 or MCB2 THEN compression bar area ≥ 1000 mm²/metre width of corbel, AND secondary horizontal reinforcement / horizontal links area ≥ 0.50 × area of main tensile reinforcement.
IF using Model Detail MCB1 (without welds) THEN main tensile reinforcement bar size should be ≤16mm. IF using Model Detail MCB2 (with welds) THEN main tensile reinforcement bar size should be ≤20mm.
IF detailing a corbel THEN two column links should be placed close to the corbel top.
IF detailing Model Detail MN1 nib links THEN link diameter must not be more than 12mm.
IF detailing Model Detail MN2 (shallow nib) THEN nib depth must not be less than 140mm, horizontal U-bar diameter must not be more than 16mm, and U-bar pitch must not be more than 250mm.
IF detailing Model Detail MN1 THEN minimum nominal overlap between reinforcement in the nib and reinforcement in the supported member = 60mm.
IF a lacer bar is used with MN2 horizontal U-bars THEN it must be wired to at least two main longitudinal bars.
